headline: OpenAI in talks to raise $30B at $1.4T valuation
summary: The ChatGPT maker is reportedly seeking a massive pre-IPO funding round, aiming for a staggering $1.4 trillion valuation.
details: OpenAI is reportedly in discussions with investors to secure at least $30 billion in a pre-IPO funding round. This would place the company's valuation at approximately $1.4 trillion, according to Bloomberg.

This significant fundraising effort comes as investors show strong interest in the ChatGPT maker ahead of its anticipated public market debut. OpenAI's run-rate revenue has seen a substantial 70% increase since July, reaching $40 billion in August.
The company's valuation has seen rapid growth, having previously raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion valuation. This latest round is intended to serve as a bridge to its eventual IPO.

Despite the push for funding, CEO Sam Altman has recently stated that an IPO will not occur in 2026. He cited prioritizing AI safety as the reason, emphasizing the need to mitigate potential existential risks associated with advanced AI.
Altman expressed concerns about the potential dangers of AI, stating, "I think it is unacceptable to be taking like a 10% chance of killing everybody by the end of the decade."
caption:
OpenAI is reportedly in talks to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation.

OpenAI is reportedly in discussions with investors to secure at least $30 billion in a pre-IPO funding round. This would place the company's valuation at approximately $1.4 trillion, according to Bloomberg.

This significant fundraising effort comes as investors show strong interest in the ChatGPT maker ahead of its anticipated public market debut. OpenAI's run-rate revenue has seen a substantial 70% increase since July, reaching $40 billion in August.

The company's valuation has seen rapid growth, having previously raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion valuation. This latest round is intended to serve as a bridge to its eventual IPO.

Despite the push for funding, CEO Sam Altman has recently stated that an IPO will not occur in 2026. He cited prioritizing AI safety as the reason, emphasizing the need to mitigate potential existential risks associated with advanced AI.

Altman expressed concerns about the potential dangers of AI, stating, "I think it is unacceptable to be taking like a 10% chance of killing everybody by the end of the decade."
